findings.assertion: The September 19 earthquake devastated multiple central neighborhoods; the event must be distinguished from its September 20 aftershock and not dated by later commemorations.
findings.period: Earthquake, city response and environmental history
findings.source_locator: El Universal 20 Sep 1985 scanned p.1 masthead/headline; NIST 1987 abstract
findings.limitations: Do not conflate local felt time, reported magnitude scales or later casualty estimates; original instrument record not inspected.

findings.assertion: The day-after front page printed provisional claims of more than 3,000 deaths and 50,000 displaced families; these numbers document contemporaneous uncertainty, not verified final totals.
findings.source_locator: El Universal Friday 20 Sep 1985 scanned p.1 headline and subheads
findings.limitations: The photographed newspaper is primary evidence of what was reported, not validation of estimates or military orders included in subheads.

findings.assertion: Accounts from UNAM and contemporaneous sociological research distinguish volunteer rescue during the immediate emergency from later organized housing claims.
themes: grassroots rescue, aid and disaster governance
findings.source_locator: UNAM CCUT M68 2022 lines 13–25; Massolo 1986 publisher abstract
findings.limitations: Do not reduce response to absolute government absence; timing, degree and geographic distribution need original reports.

findings.assertion: Massolo identifies the First Forum of Disaster Victims at Tlatelolco's Auditorio 5 de Mayo on 24 October 1985 as the founding moment of the Coordinadora Única de Damnificados.
themes: formation of Coordinadora Única de Damnificados
findings.source_locator: Massolo 1986 abstract explicitly dates First Foro de Damnificados to Oct 24 in auditorio 5 de Mayo; Marván/Cuevas journal metadata only
findings.limitations: Exact attendees and program, organizational continuity, and exact auditorium footprint require full 1986 study and archival records.

findings.assertion: An April 1986 federal publication explicitly ties rebuilding standards in three D.F. delegations to the 12 October 1985 Renovación Habitacional Popular initiative (published 14 October) and discusses neighborhood continuity and housing rights.
findings.period: Housing reconstruction legislation and land tenure
themes: popular housing decree and rebuilding norms
geographies: Cuauhtémoc / Venustiano Carranza / Gustavo A. Madero
findings.source_locator: DOF 22 Apr 1986, preamble and Article PRIMERO; October 1985 predecessor decree referenced
findings.limitations: The earlier decree itself was not directly read; 1986 rules are primary evidence of the later program, not proof of every implemented outcome.

findings.assertion: A September 20 contemporary front page labels the Nuevo León collapse in Tlatelolco; UNAM catalogs independent photographs credited to Enrique Bordes Mangel and Marco Antonio Cruz.
themes: collapsed Edificio Nuevo León and photographic witness
findings.source_locator: 20 Sep 1985 El Universal scanned p.1 photo caption Nuevo León; UNAM IIE exhibition catalog caption 33; UNAM M68 image credit
findings.limitations: Original construction/collapse engineering dossier, precise rebuilding footprint and permission to display photographs remain unverified.

findings.assertion: The housing movement has an identifiable gathering place—the Auditorio 5 de Mayo—rather than being only a general story of anonymous volunteers.
findings.period: Community organizing in the housing complex
themes: Auditorio 5 de Mayo as forum venue
findings.limitations: Do not plot a modern pin or promise access until address, survival, current use and visiting policy checked.

findings.assertion: UNAM's photographic exhibit describes the post-earthquake removal of Diego Rivera's Sueño de una tarde dominical en la Alameda Central from the Hotel del Prado context, with subsequent Museo Mural Diego Rivera construction.
themes: Hotel del Prado mural relocation context
findings.limitations: Chronology of temporary placement, new museum inauguration, conservation intervention and rights of artwork reproduction require dedicated corroboration.

findings.assertion: Hotel Regis appears in contemporaneous earthquake reporting and in a UNAM archival photograph credited to Enrique Bordes Mangel, a promising then/now pairing.
findings.period: Hotel collapse and historical photographic witness
themes: Hotel Regis original site and rescue photography
geographies: Avenida Juárez, precise historic footprint unverified
findings.source_locator: El Universal 20 Sep 1985 scanned p.1 subhead Hotel Regis; UNAM IIE opening caption Los últimos momentos del Hotel Regis
findings.limitations: Do not infer present-day property boundaries, installation access or photographic reuse rights without the original map and catalog record.

findings.assertion: A 1986 sociological article studies women's employment among persons reached by IIS-UNAM's Encuesta de Damnificados and highlights women heads of household and garment workers.
findings.period: Survey-based social history and unequal impacts
themes: women's precarious employment in disaster displacement
geographies: Mexico City shelters and camps; individual sites unresolved
findings.source_locator: de Barbieri/Guzmán 1986 journal abstract pp.59–101, publisher lines 40–51
findings.limitations: Abstract does not expose sample design or estimates: no quantified relative harm or inferred citywide gender rates approved.

findings.assertion: NBS/USGS dispatched engineers and a seismologist to document ground shaking, design provisions and observed building/foundation failures, offering technical evidence separate from social-memory accounts.
themes: ground motion, structural collapse and design-code testing
findings.source_locator: NIST NBS BSS165 1987 publication abstract; original El Universal photo page 1
findings.limitations: Full 1987 structural report, engineering drawings and sediment amplification measurements not examined; no building-specific failure mechanism should be asserted.
